ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an ideal operational amplifier circuit, with input voltage ui connected to the non-inverting input terminal (+) of the op-amp. The output terminal is labeled uo, and is directly fed back to the inverting input terminal (-) through a wire. The node where the inverting input terminal is located is also connected to ground through a resistor. Reasoning: An ideal op-amp under negative feedback satisfies V- = V+. Since the non-inverting terminal voltage V+ = ui, and the inverting terminal is the same node as the output terminal uo through the wire, V- = uo. Therefore uo = ui, and the voltage gain Au = uo/ui = 1. The grounded resistor is only equivalent to a load on the output node and does not change the closed-loop gain of the ideal voltage follower.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: ui is applied to the op-amp non-inverting input, while the output node uo is fed back directly to the inverting input; the resistor only connects that node to ground and does not change the ideal op-amp input relation. Apply the ideal negative-feedback rule V- = V+. Because V+ = ui and V- is the same node as uo, conclude uo = ui and therefore the voltage gain is 1.

method.method_draft: Recognize the diagram as a non-inverting amplifier in the special voltage-follower form: the signal ui enters the + input and the output is fed directly back to the - input. Treat the resistor from the - node to ground as Rg and the direct feedback wire as Rf = 0. Substitute into Av = 1 + Rf/Rg to obtain Av = 1.

This is distinct but closely related because both rely on ideal negative-feedback op-amp behavior.
planner_metadata.image_role: Identify from the image that ui is connected to the + input and the - input is connected directly to the output node uo; there is also a resistor from the feedback node to ground, corresponding to the ground leg of a non-inverting amplifier with zero feedback resistance between output and the inverting input.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt only to select the desired output: the numerical voltage amplification factor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has closed-loop voltage gain Av = 1 + Rf/Rg, where Rf is the resistance from output to inverting input and Rg is from inverting input to ground. In the shown circuit the output-to-inverting-input connection is a short, so Rf = 0, giving Av = 1 + 0/Rg = 1. Equivalently, it is a unity-gain buffer.
